newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Fr franc vol bid amid French poll nerves.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Fr franc vol bid amid French poll nerves.

text.p: French franc vols were bid higher in European morning trading, boosted by market concern about political uncertainty in the run-up to an expected snap election in France, traders said.
One-month mark/French franc vols rose from levels of around 0.5 percent in the middle of last week to 1.4/1.8 in European morning trade. Dollar/French franc vols also firmed to 8.3/8.6 from 8.0/8.4.
"Mark/French franc vols are pretty bid and are likely to be bid up with any spike higher in the (mark/franc) spot," said Kevin Murphy, options trader at Banque Nationale de Paris.
French President Jacques Chirac will broadcast to the nation at 1800 GMT amid mounting speculation that he will announce an early general election in late May or early June.

Options traders said speculation about possible election dates was intense and had pushed up vols on short-dated options with maturities around May 25, June 1, and June 8, the dates many options traders expect to be set for the two-stage election.

The main risk for French financial markets is that the ruling centre-right coalition, committed to European monetary union, loses to a Socialist-led alliance which might struggle to reconcile deficit-cutting policies with a desire to stimulate growth and reduce record unemployment, analysts said.
Once an election is called, any swing in the opinion polls towards the Socialists would swell implied volatility, said Murphy at BNP.

"It will be a very information-driven market when the election is called, and if the Socialists get ahead in the poll I wouldn't be surprised to see vols back above three percent in mark/Paris," said Murphy.
An opinion poll published on Monday in Le Figaro newspaper showed France's ruling centre-right coalition would lose about 150 seats but retain a parliamentary majority if elections were held now.

The French franc was at 3.3743/48 per mark, its lowest level in a month and down from 3.3694/99 in late European trading on Friday, after rising to its highest level since June 1993 at 3.3615 last Tuesday.

Even though the franc has weakened amid election speculation it remained well supported. Political uncertainty would rule out any further easing in interest rates but the franc would have to fall a lot further before the Bank of France would hike rates, traders said.
"The franc is holding up reasonably well in the face of the political uncertainty," said an options trader at a U.S. bank here. "The options market is naturally concerned but not in a panic."
The risk reversal on one-month 25 delta mark/French franc options moved higher in favour of mark calls at 0.5/1.0 percent, traders said.
French bond and interest rate futures fell sharply on Monday, with the short end taking the biggest hit, and the blue-chip CAC-40 index was down over one percent at the open amid election fears.

Analysts said Chirac's rationale behind calling an early election was to get it out of the way now rather than have to campaign next year at a time of possibly unpopular austerity measures to enable France to qualify for a single European currency. The French election was orginally due in March 1998.
